concept: Graph-Guided Context Compaction and Dynamic Window Assembly
summary: Dynamic token budgeting, topological sort serialization, and geodesic path pruning for packing subgraphs into limited LLM context windows.

related.concept: Multi-Hop Subgraph Context Expansion and Traversal
Hybrid Dense, Sparse, and Graph Retrieval Fusion
Cross-Encoder Graph Re-Ranking and Terminal Path Validation

facts.text: Topological sorting of extracted subgraph contexts produces causal, dependency-ordered prompt serialization that minimizes attention dispersion in autoregressive language models.
Redundancy-aware graph compaction collapses intermediate bridging nodes while preserving geodesic paths between query entities and factual targets, reducing prompt token consumption by 35%–50%.
Dynamic context window budgeting assigns token allocations proportionally to graph community centrality and node degree, preventing peripheral entity noise from displacing core factual evidence.
